question.prompt: What is the sum of all real numbers \(x\) for which the median of the numbers \(4,\) \(6,\) \(8,\) \(17,\) and \(x\) is equal to the mean of those five numbers?

solutions.title: Split by the median
solutions.explanation:
The median is the third number after sorting, so its value changes only as \(x\) passes \(6\) and \(8\). The mean is
\[
\frac{4+6+8+17+x}{5}=\frac{x+35}{5}.
\]
Consider the three disjoint cases, which cover every real \(x\).

If \(x<6\), the median is \(6\). Equality with the mean requires
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=6
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x+35=30
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=-5.
\]
This satisfies \(x<6\).

If \(6\le x\le8\), the median is \(x\). Then
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 35=4x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=\frac{35}{4}>8,
\]
which does not belong to this case.

If \(x>8\), the median is \(8\). Then
\[
\frac{x+35}{5}=8
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x=5,
\]
which also falls outside its case.

Thus the only valid value is \(-5\), so the requested sum is \(\boxed{-5}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
